title: Artificial Intelligence Lab
description: The AI course, in Python. Two weeks of Python for someone who already codes, then agents, uninformed and heuristic search, expert systems, and after the midterm the classic machine-learning models from linear regression to multi-layer networks. No lab manuals yet: each lab here is built from the outline and the tasks posted on Google Classroom, and adapted when manuals arrive.
textbook: Russell & Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach (4th ed). Reference: Hemalatha, Artificial Intelligence Laboratory Manual (Python-Based).

modules.title: Lab 01: Python for someone who already codes
modules.outline: Python introduction: basics, loops, functions. Built from the outline alone (no manual or task was posted); here it is the traps a JavaScript or Java developer hits in their first hour of Python.

lessons.title: Python for someone who already codes
lessons.objective: predict the output of Python snippets that trip up JavaScript and Java developers: truthiness, half-open ranges, floor division, mutable defaults, for/else, and multiple return values.

modules.title: Lab 02: Tuples, sets, lists, dictionaries
modules.outline: Python data structures: tuples, sets, lists and dictionaries. Class Task 1 (in lab, due 21 Sep) and Lab Task 1 (home, due 22 Sep) both exercise them on student, course, book and shopping-cart records.

lessons.title: Choosing a collection
lessons.objective: pick the right one of tuple, list, set and dict for a job, explain mutability and hashability, and use set algebra, comprehensions, dict.get and key functions without looking them up.

lessons.title: Class Task 1 and Lab Task 1, worked
lessons.objective: write all ten task answers from scratch, then compare with idiomatic solutions and the edge cases each question hides.

modules.title: Lab 03: Simple-reflex and goal-based agents
modules.outline: Implementation of simple-reflex and goal-based agents. No manual yet; built on the Russell and Norvig vacuum world that AI lecture 2 uses, so the code mirrors the theory. Adapt when the manual is posted.

lessons.title: A reflex vacuum agent in Python
lessons.objective: write an environment class, a percept, and a condition-action agent, run the sense-act loop, and score it with a performance measure.

lessons.title: Giving the agent memory and a goal
lessons.objective: turn the reflex agent into one that keeps a model of the world, tests a goal, and stops, and explain in code terms how the two agent types differ.

modules.title: Lab 04: Uninformed search, BFS and DFS
modules.outline: Uninformed search: breadth-first and depth-first search. No manual yet. Queue versus stack, the reached set, path reconstruction, and the hand-tracing questions exams ask.

lessons.title: BFS and DFS: a queue or a stack
lessons.objective: implement BFS and DFS in Python from one template, trace the frontier by hand, and say which one finds the shallowest path and why.

lessons.title: Search tracing checkpoint
lessons.objective: write the expansion order and returned path for BFS and DFS on unseen graphs, under the tie-breaking rule the question states.

modules.title: Lab 07: Expert systems, forward and backward chaining
modules.outline: Expert systems using Python, forward chaining, backward chaining.

modules.title: Lab 14: Single-layer neural networks
modules.outline: Classification using single-layer artificial neural networks.

modules.title: Lab 15: Multi-layer neural networks
modules.outline: Classification using multi-layer artificial neural networks.
